newsitem.title: USA: Brazil must build on stabilization program - IMF.
newsitem.headline: Brazil must build on stabilization program - IMF.

text.p: Brazil must build on the success of its Plano Real stabilization program by carrying out critical public sector reforms, International Monetary Fund managing director Michel Camdessus said Thursday.
"The Plano Real cannot deliver more than what it was designed for," Camdessus told a news conference as events associated with the annual IMF/World Bank meetings got underway.

"We think that now there is a lot to do in the reform of the social security system, of the public administration, the tax system, and a deepening of the privatization effort to allow the improvement of the fiscal position, which over the medium term will be critical for the lasting success of this program," he added.

Brazil launched the Plano Real in 1994 to stabilize its currency and defeat crippingly high inflation. The rates plummeted but President Fernando Henrique Cardoso has had trouble in winning congressional approval for other reforms.

Camdessus noted that Brazil had recently completed the privatization of a power utility in Rio de Janeiro but said that more would have to be done. "I hope that the government and the Congress will able to continue in this direction."
